title: Apply Operations to Make String Empty

Apply Operations to Make String Empty You are given a string s. Consider performing the following operation until s becomes empty: - For every alphabet character from 'a' to 'z', remove the first occurrence of that character in s (if it exists). For example, let initially s = "aabcbbca". We do the following operations: - Remove the underlined characters s = "aabcbbca". The string just before the last operation is "abcd". Constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^5 s consists only of lowercase English letters. """ class Solution: def lastNonEmptyString(self, s: str) -> str: pass sol = Solution() print(sol.lastNonEmptyString("aabcbbca")) # "ba" # assert sol.lastNonEmptyString("aabcbbca") == "ba" # assert sol.lastNonEmptyString("abcd") == "abcd"
solution: """ URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/apply-operations-to-make-string-empty/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr 3039. Apply Operations to Make String Empty You are given a string s. Consider performing the following operation until s becomes empty: - For every alphabet character from 'a' to 'z', remove the first occurrence of that character in s (if it exists). For example, let initially s = "aabcbbca". We do the following operations: - Remove the underlined characters s = "aabcbbca". The resulting string is s = "abbca". - Remove the underlined characters s = "abbca". The resulting string is s = "ba". - Remove the underlined characters s = "ba". The resulting string is s = "". Return the value of the string s right before applying the last operation. In the example above, answer is "ba". Example 1: Input: s = "aabcbbca" Output: "ba" Explanation: Explained in the statement. Example 2: Input: s = "abcd" Output: "abcd" Explanation: We do the following operation: - Remove the underlined characters s = "abcd". The resulting string is s = "". The string just before the last operation is "abcd". Constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^5 s consists only of lowercase English letters. """ class Solution: def lastNonEmptyString(self, s: str) -> str: from collections import deque # Positions of each character in s pos = [deque() for _ in range(26)] for i, ch in enumerate(s): pos[ord(ch) - ord("a")].append(i) removed = [False] * len(s) last_string = s while True: removed_this_round = [] for i in range(26): if pos[i]: idx = pos[i].popleft() removed[idx] = True removed_this_round.append(idx) if not removed_this_round: # No characters removed, string is empty break # Build the string after removal current_string = [] for i, ch in enumerate(s): if not removed[i]: current_string.append(ch) if not current_string: # The string just before last operation is last_string return last_string last_string = "".join(current_string) sol = Solution() print(sol.lastNonEmptyString("aabcbbca")) # "ba" assert sol.lastNonEmptyString("aabcbbca") == "ba" assert sol.lastNonEmptyString("abcd") == "abcd"
